summary: Lamech calls the injury he suffered a פֶּצַע and pairs it with a bruise. The law uses the same noun in its provision for wound for wound.

senses.definition: A wound or bodily injury inflicted by a blow.

evidence.note: Lamech sets “for my wound” alongside “for my bruise” as he tells his wives why he killed.
The law pairs wound with wound, just as it pairs burn with burn and bruise with bruise.

parallels.note: The second line names a bruise where the first names a wound.
